name: Launchpad for Cowork recipe index
note: Weights order the recipes and are never shown. Credit figures are planning ranges, not quotes.

recipes.title: Month-end variance commentary
recipes.job_to_be_done: As someone who closes the month, I want a sourced first draft of the variance commentary in my house style so that review starts from evidence, not a blank page.
recipes.what_you_get: A first draft for every material line, in your template, each with its source and an evidence status.
recipes.why_you_if: For you if you write the monthly variance commentary.
recipes.choice_description: A sourced first draft in your house style
recipes.example_alt: Example: October variance commentary, a draft for review with an evidence status on every material line and two questions drafted for owners, not sent
would_you_like: A draft of every material line in your house style, each with its source and an evidence status.
Questions to owners drafted and grouped by owner, ready for you to send or not.
steps: Register the inputs for the period and tie them out to the control totals.
Apply your materiality rule to the variance table worked out by the script.
Draft one entry per material line in your house style, with its source.
Give every entry an evidence status: Supported, Partly supported, Not supported or Awaiting owner.
Draft one question per gap, grouped by owner, and send nothing.
Assemble the draft in your template, marked as a draft for review.
inputs: Locked-period ledger extract or trial balance
The variance workbook, if you keep one
outputs: A list of open questions by owner, drafted not sent
A register of the sources used

credits_per_run.label: planning range
credits_per_run.basis: Planning range from comparable designs. Replace it with your own measured runs.

measure_map.Missed deadlines: Packs ready on the planned day
measure_map.Contractors or overtime: Contractor and overtime spend at month-end

helpers.name: close-inputs-check
helpers.purpose: Registers and ties out the inputs

helpers.name: variance-owner-questions
helpers.purpose: One question per gap, grouped by owner, drafted not sent

recipes.test_approach: Run the new skill on last period's inputs and compare it line by line with the commentary that was actually sent: lines covered, the same, different with reasons, questions it would have sent, and figures changed, which must be none.

recipes.title: Budget round app
recipes.job_to_be_done: As someone running a round of submissions from a shared tracker and status emails, I want each owner to update their own line so that I can see who is late without chasing anyone.
recipes.what_you_get: An app built from your tracker's own columns: owners update their own line, and you see who is late without chasing.
recipes.why_you_if: For you if you run a round of submissions from a shared spreadsheet.
recipes.choice_description: Owners update their own lines; you see who is late
recipes.example_alt: Example app: a budget round with tiles for submitted, in review, overdue and gap to target, and a table of cost centres by owner and status
would_you_like: One app built from your tracker's own columns, where each owner updates their own line.
Tiles for submitted, in review, overdue and gap to target, a drafted chaser per overdue owner, and a Friday summary.
steps: Read the tracker's columns and rows, with your OK for that one file.
Map the columns: cost centre, owner, status, submitted date and value against target.
Give Cowork's App skill a precise brief built from your columns.
Show summary tiles and the overdue list, worked out by a script.
Draft one chaser per overdue owner and send nothing.
Set up a Friday summary that drafts itself for you to check.
outputs: An app built from the tracker
One drafted chaser per overdue owner, not sent
A Friday summary, drafted for you
who_decides: You decide who can use the app.

app_brief.weekly_summary: Every Friday: submitted, in review, overdue and gap to target, with the overdue owners listed, drafted for you to check.

sizing.credits_basis: No planning range yet. Measure a few weekly summaries first.

measure_map.Questions from the board or a regulator: Lines with a confirmed owner and date
measure_map.Contractors or overtime: Contractor and overtime spend during the round

blueprint.run_prompt: Draft this week's budget round summary

recipes.test_approach: Run the weekly summary on last week's tracker and compare it with the status email you actually sent: owners covered, the same, different with reasons, and figures changed, which must be none.

recipes.title: Monthly business review brief
recipes.job_to_be_done: As someone preparing for the monthly business review, I want a one-page brief the evening before so that I go in with the right questions.
recipes.what_you_get: A one-page brief the evening before: what moved since last month, the questions to put to each business, and open actions from last time.
recipes.why_you_if: For you if you prepare for a monthly business review.
recipes.choice_description: One page the evening before, with the questions to ask
recipes.example_alt: Example: one-page MBR brief for November, with what moved since last month, questions for each business and open actions from last time
would_you_like: A one-page brief the evening before each monthly business review.
What moved since last month, the questions to put to each business, and open actions from last time.
steps: Find this month's and last month's pack and forecast files by name, then read them with your OK.
Work out what moved since last month with a script.
Draft the questions to put to each business.
List the open actions from last time.
Put it on one page, ready the evening before.
You decide what to ask; nothing is sent.

sizing.credits_basis: No planning range yet. Measure a few briefs first.

blueprint.run_prompt: Prepare my brief for the {next_period} business review

recipes.test_approach: Prepare last month's brief from last month's files and compare it with what was discussed or the notes you kept: questions covered, the same, different with reasons, and figures changed, which must be none.

recipes.title: Committee paper
recipes.job_to_be_done: As a paper author, I want a full first draft in the committee's template so that the paper reaches the committee first time.
recipes.what_you_get: A full first draft in your committee's template, then a coaching review against your paper standard.
recipes.why_you_if: For you if you write papers for a board or committee.
recipes.choice_description: A full first draft, then a coaching review
recipes.example_alt: Example: committee paper front sheet with decision sought, recommendation, risks and next steps, beside a coaching review with one mandatory and two recommended findings
would_you_like: A full first draft in your committee's template: decision sought, recommendation, background, risks and next steps.
Every figure with its source and as-at date, then a coaching review with mandatory and recommended findings.
steps: Confirm the committee, the meeting date and the decision sought, asking once.
Read the template, the paper standard and the evidence you name, with your OK for each file.
Draft the front sheet first: decision sought, recommendation, background, risks and next steps.
Give every figure its source and as-at date, and write not stated where evidence is missing.
Coach the draft against your paper standard: mandatory and recommended findings, each anchored to a place in the paper.
You decide. It never declares a paper ready and never submits it.
inputs: Last cycle's paper, if this is an update
outputs: A full draft in the template
A coaching review with mandatory and recommended findings
A list of figures with sources and as-at dates
who_decides: You decide what the paper says.
measures: Papers reaching the committee first time

credits_per_run.label: planning range
credits_per_run.basis: Planning range per paper from a comparable design. Replace it with your own measured runs.

measure_map.Missed deadlines: Papers in the pack by the deadline
measure_map.Questions from the board or a regulator: Papers reaching the committee first time

helpers.name: paper-coaching-review
helpers.purpose: Coaching review against the paper standard

blueprint.run_prompt: Draft the paper for the {next_period} committee

recipes.test_approach: Draft last cycle's paper from the evidence it used and compare it with the paper that went to the committee: sections covered, the same, different with reasons, not stated gaps, and figures changed, which must be none.

sizing.credits_basis: No planning range yet. Measure a few runs first.

measure_map.Missed deadlines: Drafts ready on the planned day
